subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep security audit treat plugin manifests over 1 MiB as unavailable and emit `plugins.code_safety.manifest_parse_error` while continuing directory scanning?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but selecting the cutoff and accepting reduced declared-entrypoint coverage for oversized manifests is a security-policy choice rather than a correctness question automation can settle.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Accept the proposed cap and warning behavior as a proportionate defense against unbounded audit reads.

options.title: Define a different manifest contract
options.body: Choose a different shared maximum or diagnostic category, then update the helper and boundary tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed cap and warning behavior as a proportionate defense against unbounded audit reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is ownership of repository security policy and published security-boundary decisions.
